title: REQ · Coding agent providers: mock and Claude Code CLI adapter with restricted permissions and no shell interpolation
summary: Provider interface, mock provider and a Claude CLI adapter built on an injectable command runner
description: Context: community text is untrusted. Desired behavior: provider.Provider has Run(ctx, workDir, prompt) (cost, output, err); Mock returns a deterministic result and is flagged as mock; Claude builds an argument slice for the configured command with restricted permission flags, runs it with Dir=workDir through an injected Exec function, and sends the structured prompt on stdin, never in a shell string. Why: safe coding-agent invocation.
acceptance_criteria: Given the mock provider, when Run is called, then it returns its configured cost and output and Mock() is true
Given the Claude adapter, when Run is called with a prompt containing shell metacharacters, then the argument slice contains no prompt text and the prompt is passed on stdin
Given the Claude adapter, then args include print mode and an explicit allowed-tools list excluding Bash and the working directory equals workDir
Given the command fails or ctx is cancelled, then Run returns an error wrapping the cause

out_of_scope: Running the real Claude binary in tests

technical_constraints: exec.CommandContext with an argument slice; never sh -c
definition_of_done: Providers satisfy the runner Agent signature
